docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Build a clean admin panel for your Go models.

Go Admin uses GORM metadata and a small registration API to generate CRUD screens, dashboards, authentication, audit logs, filters, actions, and exports.

Start building Run the demo API docs

docs.title: Why Go Admin
docs.text:
Fast setup

Register a GORM model, expose fields, and mount the admin router.

Built-in auth

Session-based login with admin users, roles, permissions, and bcrypt passwords.

Useful workflows

Batch actions, CSV export, search filters, custom pages, and audit logging.

Portable UI

Templates and styles are embedded into the Go binary with `go:embed`.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: go get github.com/go-packs/go-admin

docs.title: Minimal Example
docs.text:
adm := admin.NewRegistry(db)

adm.Register(Product{}).
    SetGroup("Inventory").
    RegisterField("ID", "ID", true).
    RegisterField("Name", "Product Name", false).
    RegisterField("Price", "Price", false)

http.Handle("/admin/", server.NewRouter(adm))
log.Fatal(http.ListenAndServe(":8080", nil))

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: The repository includes a runnable demo app under examples/.

docs.title: Run The Demo
docs.text:
go run ./examples

The demo creates a local SQLite database at:

examples/demo.db

Open the admin panel:

http://localhost:8080/admin

Sign in with:

Email: admin@example.com
Password: password123

docs.title: What The Demo Shows
docs.text:
• Admin users, roles, permissions, sessions, and audit logs.
  • Product and user resources.
  • Select fields, number fields, image fields, and decorators.
  • Has-many and belongs-to associations.
  • Collection actions, member actions, and batch actions.
  • Dashboard charts and custom pages.

docs.title: Reset Demo Data
docs.text:
Stop the server, delete the generated database, then run the example again.

rm examples/demo.db
go run ./examples

The database file is intentionally ignored by Git. Users should generate local data when they run examples.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text: Go packages are published by pushing a public Git repository and tagging semantic versions.

docs.title: Repository Path
docs.text:
The module path in go.mod must match the public repository URL.

module github.com/go-packs/go-admin

For this module path, the GitHub repository should be:

https://github.com/go-packs/go-admin

docs.title: Release Checklist
docs.text:
• Keep README.md, USAGE.md, examples/, tests, CI, and LICENSE.
  • Do not commit generated databases, uploads, build output, local caches, secrets, or .env files.
  • Run go test ./....
  • Commit the release-ready changes.
  • Tag a version such as v0.1.0.

docs.title: Publish A Version
docs.text:
git add .
git commit -m "Prepare open source release"
git push origin main

git tag v0.1.0
git push origin v0.1.0

Users can install the tagged release with:

go get github.com/go-packs/go-admin@v0.1.0

docs.title: Package Documentation
docs.text:
Go API documentation appears on pkg.go.dev after the package is public:

https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-packs/go-admin

docs.title: Showcase Documentation
docs.text:
This docs site is published with GitHub Pages. After the workflow runs, the site URL is:

https://go-packs.github.io/go-admin/

If the repository lives under a different GitHub user or organization, update site_url, repo_url, and repo_name in mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: This page creates a small admin app with SQLite and one Product resource.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
go get github.com/go-packs/go-admin
go get gorm.io/driver/sqlite gorm.io/gorm

docs.title: Create main.go
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "log"
    "net/http"

    admin "github.com/go-packs/go-admin"
    "github.com/go-packs/go-admin/server"
    "gorm.io/driver/sqlite"
    "gorm.io/gorm"
)

type Product struct {
    ID    uint `gorm:"primaryKey"`
    Name  string
    Price float64
}

func main() {
    db, err := gorm.Open(sqlite.Open("admin.db"), &gorm.Config{})
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    db.AutoMigrate(
        &Product{},
        &admin.AdminUser{},
        &admin.Permission{},
        &admin.Session{},
        &admin.AuditLog{},
    )

    adm := admin.NewRegistry(db)
    adm.Register(Product{}).
        SetGroup("Inventory").
        RegisterField("ID", "ID", true).
        RegisterField("Name", "Product Name", false).
        RegisterField("Price", "Price", false).
        SetFieldType("Price", "number")

    http.Handle("/admin/", server.NewRouter(adm))
    log.Println("Admin panel running at http://localhost:8080/admin")
    log.Fatal(http.ListenAndServe(":8080", nil))
}

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
go run .

Open:

http://localhost:8080/admin

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Add an admin user with admin.AdminUser and SetPassword.
  • Register more resources with adm.Register.
  • Add filters with scopes, custom behavior with actions, and dashboard metrics with charts.

docs.title: Usage Guide
docs.text: This guide covers the main extension points in github.com/go-packs/go-admin.

docs.title: Basic Setup
docs.text:
Create a GORM database connection, migrate your models and the built-in admin models, register resources, then mount the admin router.

db, err := gorm.Open(sqlite.Open("admin.db"), &gorm.Config{})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

db.AutoMigrate(&Product{}, &admin.AdminUser{}, &admin.Permission{}, &admin.Session{}, &admin.AuditLog{})

adm := admin.NewRegistry(db)
adm.Register(Product{}).
    SetGroup("Inventory").
    RegisterField("ID", "ID", true).
    RegisterField("Name", "Product Name", false).
    RegisterField("Price", "Price", false)

http.Handle("/admin/", server.NewRouter(adm))
log.Fatal(http.ListenAndServe(":8080", nil))

docs.title: Resources And Fields
docs.text:
Register a model with Register, then describe which fields should appear in the admin UI.

adm.Register(Product{}).
    SetGroup("Products").
    RegisterField("ID", "ID", true).
    RegisterField("Name", "Product Name", false).
    RegisterField("Price", "Price", false).
    SetFieldType("Price", "number")

Use SetIndexFields, SetShowFields, and SetEditFields when each view needs a different field list.

docs.title: Field Types
docs.text:
Fields default to text inputs. You can customize a field with SetFieldType.

adm.Register(User{}).
    RegisterField("Role", "Role", false).
    SetFieldType("Role", "select", "admin", "editor", "viewer")

Common field types include text, number, select, and image.

docs.title: Decorators
docs.text:
Decorators customize how values render in list and detail views.

adm.Register(Product{}).
    RegisterField("Price", "Price", false).
    SetDecorator("Price", func(value interface{}) template.HTML {
        return template.HTML(fmt.Sprintf("<strong>$%.2f</strong>", value.(float64)))
    })

docs.title: Associations
docs.text:
Use HasMany and BelongsTo to connect registered resources.

adm.Register(Product{}).
    HasMany("ProductInfo", "Technical Specifications", "ProductInfo", "ProductID")

adm.Register(ProductInfo{}).
    BelongsTo("ProductID", "Parent Product", "Product", "ID")

docs.title: Scopes
docs.text:
Scopes add predefined filters to resource list pages.

adm.Register(User{}).
    AddScope("admins", "Admins", func(db *gorm.DB) *gorm.DB {
        return db.Where("role = ?", "admin")
    })

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Member actions run against one record. Collection actions run from the resource page.

adm.Register(Product{}).
    AddCollectionAction("discount", "Apply 10% Discount", func(res *admin.Resource, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        db.Model(&Product{}).Where("price > ?", 0).Update("price", gorm.Expr("price * 0.9"))
        http.Redirect(w, r, "/admin/Product", http.StatusSeeOther)
    })

docs.title: Batch Actions
docs.text:
Batch actions run against selected record IDs.

adm.Register(Product{}).
    AddBatchAction("batch_delete", "Delete Selected", func(res *admin.Resource, ids []string, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        db.Where("id IN ?", ids).Delete(&Product{})
        http.Redirect(w, r, "/admin/Product", http.StatusSeeOther)
    })

docs.title: Dashboard Charts
docs.text:
Charts appear on the dashboard and return labels plus numeric values.

adm.AddChart("Users by Role", "pie", func(db *gorm.DB) ([]string, []float64) {
    var rows []struct {
        Role  string
        Count int64
    }

    db.Model(&User{}).Select("role, count(*) as count").Group("role").Scan(&rows)

    labels := make([]string, 0, len(rows))
    values := make([]float64, 0, len(rows))
    for _, row := range rows {
        labels = append(labels, row.Role)
        values = append(values, float64(row.Count))
    }

    return labels, values
})

docs.title: Custom Pages
docs.text:
Custom pages can render arbitrary HTML through a standard http.HandlerFunc.

adm.AddPage("SystemStatus", "Administration", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    content := template.HTML(`<p>Server status: online</p>`)
    view.RenderCustomPage(adm, w, r, "System Status", content)
})

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Load optional YAML configuration from admin.yml.

conf, err := admin.LoadConfig("admin.yml")
if err == nil && conf != nil {
    adm.SetConfig(conf)
}

Example:

site_title: "My Admin"
default_per_page: 10
